title: Cadence-based credit surge + in-app education to lift PLG conversion and surface SQ preparedness
creator: Maya Patel
description: Hypothesis: instead of a single upfront credit allotment, a time-cadence credit pulse (+ targeted educational touchpoints) will increase activation velocity and conversion to paid plans while keeping unit cost predictable. We will run a randomized experiment where low-touch signups receive staggered credit surges at defined timepoints (day 0, day 3, day 10) combined with contextual micro-education (short guide snippets and one contextual CTA) versus the current baseline of a one-off credit allotment. A secondary objective is to surface customers likely to require an enterprise contract or Security Questionnaire (SQ) earlier by observing high sustained usage after pulses, allowing a proactive sales/SQ workflow.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Primary metric: 14-day paid conversion rate increases by >=12% relative to baseline with p<0.05. 2) Secondary metrics: 30-day retention improves by >=8% OR median time-to-first-paid reduces by >=2 days. 3) No more than a 10% increase in average cost-per-trial (tokens spent) for the experimental cohort vs baseline. 4) Automated SQ flag triggers for >3k tokens/day sustained usage and a documented handoff to sales in >=90% of flagged cases.
experiment_design: Cohort: new free-tier signups over a 4-week window. Randomization unit: account_id. Variants: CONTROL (one-off 1,000 credits at signup); VAR_A (pulse 400/400/200 on day 0/3/10 + contextual tooltips after each pulse); VAR_B (pulse 200/400/600 with an educational mini-flow before the largest pulse + upgrade CTA at 70% consumption). Instrumentation: event schema for credit_awarded, credit_used, tooltip_shown, upgrade_cta_shown, sq_flagged. Sample size: 12k accounts (4k per arm) to power to the primary metric. Duration: 28 days per cohort. Safety net: rate-limit experimental credit disbursement if an account exceeds fraud heuristics.
rollout_plan: Week 0: Feature flag gated rollout to internal QA + 50 test accounts. Week 1: Canary 5% of new signups. Week 2: Ramp to 50% if no safety triggers (fraud, cost spike, support volume). Week 3: Run to completion and capture final metrics. Post-experiment: If positive, create rollout ticket with Dedicated capacity cost model and updated limits. If negative, run follow-up smaller-bandwidth variants (e.g., different pulse size).
notes_and_decisions:
- Decided to gate the largest pulse behind a short educational step to balance cost and product value.
- PM/Eng trade-off: prefer smaller frequent pulses to reduce spike-induced capacity pressure; engineering prefers day-level cadence to avoid per-minute cron overhead.
- Security: SQ flag threshold set to 3k tokens/day after consulting with Legal and Sales; this will surface accounts for proactive contract discussion.
- Support: require templated flows for common questions (billing, token accounting) to reduce ticket churn.
- Cost modeling: Finance asked to include per-variant projected marginal GPU costs; initial estimate attached in Confluence doc.
- Observability: require an SLO check for token churn and a rollback policy if average cost-per-trial increases >15%.
progress_updates: 2026-02-22: PRD drafted and reviewed with Growth + Sales. 2026-02-28: Experiment tracking events defined; ENG assigned instrumentation tasks. 2026-03-04: Design mocks iteration 2 completed; accessibility review started. 2026-03-08: Canary feature flag built; internal QA begun with 50 test accounts. 2026-03-12: Canary at 5% live; initial telemetry looks stable but support volume up 12% for tooltip-related questions (action: ship micro-FAQ).
risks_and_mitigations:
Risk: credit abuse leading to outsized cost. Mitigation: aggressive fraud heuristics, rate-limits, and per-account daily caps.
Risk: prompting users too frequently may lower LTV. Mitigation: limit CTAs to one strong upgrade prompt per account per 7 days.
Risk: early enterprise SQ churn if flagged incorrectly. Mitigation: human-in-the-loop verification for first 10 flagged accounts and a standardized outreach template.
